cards.title: Canonical plugin.yml for a Paper 1.21 plugin (name/main/version/api-version/commands/permissions)
cards.notes: plugin.yml goes in src/main/resources (root of the final jar). CLASSIC MISTAKES: (1) missing api-version → Paper logs a 'legacy plugin' warning and enables legacy material compat — always set api-version: '1.21' (quote it so YAML doesn't parse it as the float 1.21); (2) main must be the exact fully-qualified class name of the JavaPlugin subclass or the plugin fails to load; (3) every command you register in code MUST be declared under commands: here — otherwise getCommand("x") returns null and setExecutor throws NPE on enable; (4) in usage:, the literal token /<command> is auto-replaced by the command name; usage is what players see when onCommand returns false. The command-level 'permission:' key blocks the command BEFORE your executor runs (Bukkit sends its generic no-permission message) — for a custom denial message do the check in code instead.
cards.code:
name: ExamplePlugin
version: 1.0.0
main: com.example.exampleplugin.ExamplePlugin
api-version: '1.21'
description: Example Paper plugin skeleton
author: YourName

commands:
  hello:
    description: Greets the sender
    usage: /<command>
    aliases: [hi]
  greet:
    description: Greets another player
    usage: /<command> <player>
    permission: exampleplugin.greet

permissions:
  exampleplugin.greet:
    description: Allows /greet
    default: true
  exampleplugin.admin:
    description: Admin commands
    default: op

cards.title: Canonical main-class skeleton: JavaPlugin with onEnable/onDisable, logger and command registration
cards.notes: Class must be public, extend JavaPlugin, and match 'main:' in plugin.yml. getCommand() only finds commands DECLARED in plugin.yml — if the entry is missing it returns null, hence the requireNonNull with a clear message (fail fast at enable, not with a bare NPE). Register listeners in onEnable via getServer().getPluginManager().registerEvents(listener, this). Use getLogger() (already prefixed with the plugin name), NOT System.out. Never do heavy blocking work directly in onEnable — it blocks server startup. The lambda works because CommandExecutor is a functional interface; for real plugins prefer a separate CommandExecutor class.

cards.title: Basic command executor class with Adventure Component message
cards.notes: Register in onEnable: getCommand("hello").setExecutor(new HelloCommand()); AND declare 'hello' under commands: in plugin.yml — forgetting the yml entry is the #1 cause of NPE on enable / 'Unknown command' in game. Return true = handled; return false = Bukkit shows the usage: string from plugin.yml. Use Adventure Components — sendMessage(String) is deprecated on Paper, and legacy ChatColor codes are the old API; use net.kyori.adventure.text.format.NamedTextColor instead. Exact signature (verified, Paper 1.21.4): boolean onCommand(CommandSender sender, Command command, String label, String[] args).

cards.title: Command with arguments + tab completion (TabExecutor, online-player suggestions)
cards.notes: Register BOTH in onEnable: PluginCommand cmd = getCommand("greet"); GreetCommand exec = new GreetCommand(); cmd.setExecutor(exec); cmd.setTabCompleter(exec); — don't rely on setExecutor alone wiring the completer. Returning an EMPTY list from onTabComplete = no suggestions; returning NULL falls back to the default (online player names) — a common surprise. Always filter suggestions by the partial arg (args[args.length-1] / args[0] here) or the client shows everything. Bukkit.getPlayerExact(name) returns null if offline — always null-check. Exact signature (verified, Paper 1.21.4): List<String> onTabComplete(CommandSender sender, Command command, String label, String[] args).

cards.title: Permission check inside a command with a custom denial message (hasPermission)
cards.notes: hasPermission works on any CommandSender; the CONSOLE always passes every permission check. Declare the node under permissions: in plugin.yml with a sensible default (default: op for admin stuff) — an UNDECLARED permission node defaults to op-only. Two ways to gate a command: (a) 'permission:' key on the command in plugin.yml — blocks before your executor runs but shows Bukkit's generic denial message; (b) this in-code check — lets you send your own Component message. Don't do both unless you want the generic message to win. Return true after the denial message, otherwise the usage string is also shown.

cards.title: Permission nodes in plugin.yml: defaults (true/false/op/not op) and children
cards.notes: Valid defaults: true (everyone), false (nobody), op (operators only), 'not op' (quote it — it contains a space). A node NOT declared anywhere defaults to op. children: maps child-node -> boolean: true = granting the parent also grants the child; false = granting the parent NEGATES the child. Wildcards like exampleplugin.* are NOT automatic — declare a parent node with children explicitly (permission plugins like LuckPerms add their own wildcard handling on top). Permission managers (LuckPerms) override these defaults per group/user; the defaults here are what applies on a vanilla-permissions server.
cards.code:
permissions:
  exampleplugin.use:
    description: Basic usage
    default: true
  exampleplugin.admin:
    description: All admin tools (parent node)
    default: op
    children:
      exampleplugin.admin.reload: true
      exampleplugin.use: true
  exampleplugin.admin.reload:
    description: Reload the plugin config
    default: false
  exampleplugin.newbie:
    description: Granted to everyone who is not an operator
    default: 'not op'

cards.title: Console vs player sender handling (instanceof Player pattern match)
cards.notes: NEVER blind-cast (Player) sender — the sender can be the console, a command block, or RCON, and the cast throws ClassCastException. Java 21 pattern matching (instanceof Player player) checks and binds in one step. Only gate on Player when you genuinely need a location/inventory/world — commands that just print or mutate config should keep working from console (server owners run them from scripts). The console also receives Adventure Components fine (colors render as ANSI). If a command is player-only AND you want tab-complete/permissions too, combine this check with the TabExecutor and hasPermission patterns.

cards.title: Subcommand router pattern (/kit list|give|reload) with switch and tab completion
cards.notes: One plugin.yml command + args[0] routing beats registering many top-level commands. Always lowercase args[0] with Locale.ROOT (Turkish-locale 'I' bug). Per-subcommand permission checks go inside each case (exampleplugin.kit.reload here). Tab completion must mirror the router: args.length == 1 suggests subcommand names filtered by the typed prefix; deeper args suggest that subcommand's own arguments. Register with setExecutor AND setTabCompleter (the class implements TabExecutor). Returning false on empty args shows the usage: line from plugin.yml — write it as usage: /<command> <list|give|reload>.

cards.title: Register an event Listener in onEnable (base pattern every other event card assumes)
cards.notes: Classic failures: (1) forgetting getServer().getPluginManager().registerEvents(...) — the handler compiles but silently never fires; (2) missing @EventHandler annotation on the method — same silent failure; (3) missing api-version: '1.21' in plugin.yml — server logs a legacy-plugin warning and remaps materials; (4) registering the same listener instance twice — every event fires twice. Handler methods must be public, return void, and take exactly one event parameter. Use @EventHandler(priority = EventPriority.HIGH, ignoreCancelled = true) when you need ordering or want to skip already-cancelled events.

cards.title: PlayerJoinEvent: custom join message with Adventure Components and MiniMessage
cards.notes: Use event.joinMessage(Component) — the String setJoinMessage(String) is deprecated on Paper and subject to removal. Pass null to joinMessage(...) to hide the join message entirely. MiniMessage ships bundled with Paper (net.kyori.adventure.text.minimessage) — no extra dependency needed. NEVER splice raw player-controlled text into a MiniMessage template string (tag injection); inject it via Placeholder.component/Placeholder.unparsed as shown. Do not use legacy ChatColor codes — they don't mix with Components.

cards.title: PlayerQuitEvent: customize or hide the quit message
cards.notes: Use event.quitMessage(Component); the String setQuitMessage(String) is deprecated on Paper. Pass null to suppress the message completely (common for vanish plugins). Note: a kicked player fires PlayerKickEvent (with its own leaveMessage) AND PlayerQuitEvent — if you customize both you may double-announce. The player is still valid inside the handler, but do not schedule delayed tasks that assume they remain online.

cards.title: BlockBreakEvent: cancel breaking a block unless the player has a permission
cards.notes: Use ignoreCancelled = true so you don't fight protection plugins (WorldGuard etc.) that already cancelled the event — and so uncancelling by accident is impossible. setCancelled(true) keeps the block in the world; if instead you want the block to break but drop nothing, use event.setDropItems(false). Permissions do NOT need a plugin.yml entry to work (ops/permission plugins grant them), though you may declare defaults under a permissions: section. Send feedback with Adventure Components, not legacy ChatColor strings.

cards.title: PlayerInteractEvent: detect right-click and read the ItemStack in hand (e.g. a wand item)
cards.notes: PlayerInteractEvent fires ONCE PER HAND on right-clicks — without the getHand() == EquipmentSlot.HAND guard your code runs twice. getItem() is @Nullable (null when the hand is empty); getHand() is @Nullable (null for Action.PHYSICAL, e.g. pressure plates); getClickedBlock() is null for RIGHT_CLICK_AIR. For finer control than setCancelled(true), use setUseInteractedBlock(Event.Result.DENY) / setUseItemInHand(Event.Result.DENY) to block only one side of the interaction (e.g. let a chest open but stop the item use).

cards.title: PlayerDeathEvent: keep inventory/XP on death and set a custom death message
cards.notes: DUPE WARNING: setKeepInventory(true) does NOT clear the drop list — you MUST call event.getDrops().clear() or players keep their items AND the copies drop on the ground. Same for XP: pair setKeepLevel(true) with setDroppedExp(0). Use event.deathMessage(Component) — the String setDeathMessage(String) is deprecated on Paper. deathMessage(null) hides the message. getEntity() (and Paper's getPlayer()) already return Player on this event — no cast needed.

cards.title: AsyncChatEvent (Paper): reformat chat with a ChatRenderer and filter/cancel bad words
cards.notes: Use Paper's io.papermc.paper.event.player.AsyncChatEvent — NOT the deprecated String-based AsyncPlayerChatEvent (its %s format API is legacy). The event usually fires OFF the main thread: never touch worlds, blocks, or inventories inside the handler — schedule with getServer().getScheduler().runTask(plugin, ...) if you must. renderer(...) replaces the chat format for all viewers; ChatRenderer.viewerUnaware's lambda is (Player source, Component sourceDisplayName, Component message). To inspect the text, serialize the Component with PlainTextComponentSerializer — do not toString() it. setCancelled(true) hides the message from everyone.

cards.title: EntityDamageEvent: disable fall damage for players (filter by cause + entity type)
cards.notes: EntityDamageEvent fires for EVERY entity (mobs, armor stands, items frames...) — always instanceof-check before treating it as a Player. Filter by event.getCause() (DamageCause.FALL here; FIRE, DROWNING, VOID etc. work the same). Use ignoreCancelled = true so you don't process events another plugin (god mode, regions) already cancelled. For attacker-based damage (PvP, mob hits) listen to the EntityDamageByEntityEvent subclass instead and use getDamager(). This handler runs on the main thread — world access is safe.

cards.title: Repeating task: broadcast a message every N minutes with BukkitRunnable.runTaskTimer
cards.notes: Time is in TICKS: 20 ticks = 1 second, so minutes*60*20. runTaskTimer(plugin, delay, period): the FIRST arg after plugin is the initial delay, the second is the repeat period — swapping them is a classic bug. Keep the BukkitTask reference and cancel() it in onDisable(), otherwise /reload leaks tasks (Paper cancels plugin tasks on disable, but explicit cancel is the safe habit and required if you restart the task on config reload). Use Bukkit.broadcast(Component) — broadcastMessage(String) is deprecated on Paper. Note: on 1.21.4 the SCHEDULER methods that take a BukkitRunnable argument are deprecated (use the Runnable overloads), but calling runTaskTimer directly ON a BukkitRunnable instance, as here, is NOT deprecated.

cards.title: Delayed task: run code once after N seconds (warmup teleport) with runTaskLater
cards.notes: Delay is in TICKS (5 seconds = 100L ticks), not milliseconds — passing 5000 waits 4+ minutes. Always re-check player.isOnline() (or re-fetch via Bukkit.getPlayer(uuid)) inside the delayed body: the player can log out during the delay and acting on a stale Player reference throws or silently no-ops. runTaskLater returns a BukkitTask — store it if you need to cancel (e.g., cancel the teleport when the player moves, via a PlayerMoveEvent listener). The lambda runs on the MAIN thread, so world access (teleport) is safe; do NOT confuse with runTaskLaterAsynchronously.

cards.title: Async task for slow work (DB/HTTP), then hop back to the main thread for world access
cards.notes: THE cardinal rule: the Bukkit/Paper API (world, blocks, entities, inventories, most Player methods) is NOT thread-safe — touching it from an async task throws IllegalStateException ('Asynchronous entity/chunk access!') or silently corrupts state. Only do blocking work (JDBC, HTTP, heavy computation, file IO) async, then schedule a runTask (sync) callback for anything that touches the game. Inside the callback, RE-FETCH the player by UUID — the original Player object may belong to someone who logged off (and after a relog it is a stale entity). sendMessage on Paper is one of the few thread-safe calls, but re-fetching and doing it sync is the pattern that never breaks. Never use java.util.Timer or raw Threads for this; the scheduler ties task lifetime to the plugin.

cards.title: config.yml: ship defaults with saveDefaultConfig and read strings, ints, booleans, lists
cards.notes: You MUST ship a config.yml inside the jar at src/main/resources/config.yml, or saveDefaultConfig() throws IllegalArgumentException ('The embedded resource config.yml cannot be found'). saveDefaultConfig() only copies if plugins/<Plugin>/config.yml is missing — it never overwrites user edits. Call it BEFORE the first getConfig() read (typically first line of onEnable). getConfig() returns cached values from enable time; after a manual file edit you need reloadConfig() (see the reload-command card). getStringList returns an empty list (never null) for a missing path. YAML gotcha: unquoted values like 'yes'/'no' parse as booleans, and tabs are illegal in YAML — indent with spaces. Cache values into fields once instead of calling getConfig().getX() in hot paths.

cards.title: /myreload command that re-reads config.yml from disk with reloadConfig()
cards.notes: TWO registrations or it fails: the command must exist under commands: in plugin.yml AND be wired with getCommand("myreload").setExecutor(...) in onEnable — if the plugin.yml entry is missing, getCommand returns null and you get a NullPointerException at enable; if setExecutor is missing, the command 'exists' but does nothing. reloadConfig() only refreshes what getConfig() returns — any values you cached into fields at enable time stay stale, so re-run your loadSettings()-style method after reloading (shown below). api-version: '1.21' (quoted, else YAML parses it as a float) is required in plugin.yml on modern Paper. Messages use Adventure Components; legacy ChatColor + String sendMessage is deprecated on Paper.

cards.title: Persist per-player data in a custom playerdata.yml via YamlConfiguration
cards.notes: Never key player data by name — names change; key by UUID string. YamlConfiguration.loadConfiguration(File) returns an EMPTY config (not null, no exception) when the file doesn't exist — first run just works. save(File) throws IOException, so wrap it, and mkdirs() the data folder first: on a fresh install plugins/MyPlugin/ doesn't exist yet and save() fails. data.set(...) only mutates memory — nothing hits disk until save(). Save on PlayerQuitEvent AND in onDisable() (quit events don't fire for players online during a server stop... they do fire on stop, but onDisable is your safety net for crashes of your own listeners). For frequent saves, do the disk write async (see the async-autosave card) — save() is blocking file IO. Register the Listener or onQuit never fires.

cards.title: Per-player command cooldown with HashMap<UUID, Long> and System.currentTimeMillis
cards.notes: Key by UUID, never by Player object (leaks the entity and breaks across relogs) and never by name. Compare timestamps in millis; convert the remainder to seconds with ceiling rounding (+999/1000) so the message never says 'wait 0s' while still blocking. A plain HashMap is fine because commands run on the main thread — if you also touch the map from async tasks, switch to ConcurrentHashMap. Entries for players who never return leak slowly; optionally remove on PlayerQuitEvent or use lastUsed.entrySet().removeIf(...) periodically. The instanceof pattern (sender instanceof Player player) needs Java 16+, which Paper 1.21 (Java 21) guarantees. Remember the plugin.yml commands: entry for /kit plus getCommand("kit").setExecutor(new KitCommand()) in onEnable.

cards.title: Periodic autosave: snapshot YAML on the main thread, write to disk async
cards.notes: YamlConfiguration is NOT thread-safe: calling data.save(file) from an async task while the main thread mutates the config can corrupt the file or throw ConcurrentModificationException. The safe split: serialize with saveToString() ON the main thread (cheap, memory-only snapshot), then push only the resulting immutable String to an async task for the slow disk write. The outer timer runs sync (runTaskTimer, not runTaskTimerAsynchronously) precisely so the snapshot happens on the main thread. Also run a final SYNCHRONOUS save in onDisable() — you cannot schedule new tasks while the plugin is disabling (IllegalPluginAccessException), so call data.save(file) directly there.

cards.title: Build a custom ItemStack: Adventure display name, lore, enchantments, unbreakable, item flags
cards.notes: editMeta(Consumer) is a Paper-only convenience (returns boolean); on plain Spigot you must getItemMeta/mutate/setItemMeta. CLASSIC MISTAKE 1: display names and lore render ITALIC by default in 1.16+ — always chain .decoration(TextDecoration.ITALIC, false) or items look wrong. MISTAKE 2: legacy API — meta.setDisplayName(String) + ChatColor is deprecated on Paper; use Component overloads (displayName(Component), lore(List<Component>)). MISTAKE 3: old enchant constants were renamed in 1.20.5+ to vanilla names: DAMAGE_ALL->SHARPNESS, PROTECTION_ENVIRONMENTAL->PROTECTION, DURABILITY->UNBREAKING, DIG_SPEED->EFFICIENCY, ARROW_DAMAGE->POWER — old names do not compile on 1.21. addEnchant's third arg true bypasses the vanilla level cap. Since 1.20.5, ItemFlag.HIDE_ATTRIBUTES only hides attributes the item explicitly has (vanilla component change); HIDE_UNBREAKABLE/HIDE_ENCHANTS work as before.

cards.title: /kit command that equips armor and gives items (plugin.yml + setExecutor)
cards.notes: BOTH halves are required: the plugin.yml commands entry AND getCommand("kit").setExecutor(...) in onEnable. Missing yml entry = 'Unknown command' in game AND getCommand returns null (NPE on setExecutor); missing setExecutor = the command exists but silently does nothing. plugin.yml also needs api-version: '1.21' (quoted!) or the server applies legacy material rewriting and logs warnings. The instanceof-pattern cast (sender instanceof Player player) is the modern check — console has no inventory. setHelmet/setChestplate/etc. OVERWRITE whatever armor the player wears (it is lost); check getInventory().getHelmet() != null first if that matters. addItem returns a HashMap of leftovers when the inventory is full — see items-inv-give-overflow to drop them instead of losing them.

cards.title: Give a starter kit on first join (PlayerJoinEvent listener registered in onEnable)
cards.notes: CLASSIC MISTAKE: writing the @EventHandler method but never calling registerEvents in onEnable — the event silently never fires. The class must implement Listener (the marker interface) or registerEvents rejects it. player.hasPlayedBefore() gates the kit to the first-ever join; drop that check to give it every join. PlayerJoinEvent runs on the main thread, so inventory access is safe here — never touch inventories/worlds from an async task (BukkitScheduler.runTaskAsynchronously) or you get IllegalStateException / corruption. To customize the join message on Paper use event.joinMessage(Component) (the String setter is deprecated). No plugin.yml command entry is needed for listeners — only name/version/main/api-version.

cards.title: Custom inventory GUI menu: InventoryHolder pattern, filler glass, click handling, safe close
cards.notes: Identify YOUR menu with a custom InventoryHolder passed to Bukkit.createInventory(holder, size, Component) and instanceof-check event.getInventory().getHolder() — never compare titles (brittle, breaks with Components/translations). Size must be a multiple of 9 (9..54) or createInventory throws. CRITICAL (from the InventoryClickEvent javadoc): NEVER call player.closeInventory() or openInventory() inside an InventoryClickEvent handler — schedule it next tick with getScheduler().runTask(plugin, ...). Cancel FIRST, unconditionally, while the holder matches: this also blocks shift-clicks from the bottom inventory (event.getInventory() is always the TOP inventory of the view). Also cancel InventoryDragEvent or players can drag items into the GUI. event.getCurrentItem() is null on empty slots and getClickedInventory() is null when clicking outside the window — null-check both. Register the listener in onEnable or clicks steal items.

cards.title: Check if a player has N items and remove them (pay-with-items pattern)
cards.notes: containsAtLeast(ItemStack, amount) and removeItem(ItemStack...) both match by isSimilar (type + meta): an enchanted or renamed diamond does NOT count toward a plain-diamond cost — this is the usual 'it says I don't have the items' bug. removeItem returns HashMap<Integer, ItemStack> of what could NOT be removed; empty map = full success (amounts over 64 are handled, it drains across slots). It only touches storage contents — not armor slots or offhand. Always check-then-remove in that order on the MAIN thread; both calls in the same tick are atomic (no async race). To count rather than gate: iterate getInventory().getContents(), null-check each slot, sum amounts of stacks where isSimilar matches.

cards.title: Give items safely: drop the leftovers at the player's feet when the inventory is full
cards.notes: CLASSIC MISTAKE: calling addItem and ignoring its return value — addItem returns a HashMap<Integer, ItemStack> of everything that did NOT fit, and if you ignore it those items silently vanish (players report 'lost my kit'). Drop the leftovers with dropItemNaturally at the player's location so nothing is lost. addItem splits amounts over maxStackSize across free slots automatically. Must run on the main thread (inventory + world access). setItem(slot, stack) by contrast overwrites whatever is in that slot with no leftover semantics.

cards.title: Drop an item in the world with pickup delay, velocity and glow (Consumer pre-spawn config)
cards.notes: World.dropItemNaturally(Location, ItemStack, Consumer<? super Item>) runs the consumer BEFORE the entity spawns — use it so pickup delay / velocity / glowing apply from tick zero (configuring after the plain overload returns also works but can flicker for one tick). dropItem spawns exactly at the location with zero spread; dropItemNaturally adds a small random offset and toss velocity like a mob drop. Pickup delay is in TICKS (20 = 1 second); Item.setUnlimitedLifetime(true) on Paper prevents the 5-minute despawn. CLASSIC MISTAKE: dropping items from an async task — any world access off the main thread throws IllegalStateException on Paper; wrap in getScheduler().runTask(plugin, ...) if you computed something async.

cards.title: Register a custom shaped crafting recipe (ShapedRecipe + NamespacedKey)
cards.notes: Register in onEnable. NamespacedKey must be lowercase [a-z0-9_-] or the constructor throws. Every non-space character used in shape() MUST get a setIngredient or addRecipe throws; a space is an empty cell; all rows must be the same length (1-3 chars, 1-3 rows). CLASSIC MISTAKE: on /reload, addRecipe with an already-registered key throws IllegalStateException — remove it in onDisable (Bukkit.removeRecipe(key)) or guard with Bukkit.getRecipe(key) == null. Players who joined before registration may not SEE the recipe in the recipe book until player.discoverRecipe(key) (the recipe still crafts either way). For an ingredient that must match custom meta (not just Material), use recipe.setIngredient('X', new RecipeChoice.ExactChoice(customStack)). The result ItemStack keeps its Component display name in the crafted output.

cards.title: /setspawn + /spawn commands with the location persisted in config.yml (async, cross-world safe teleport)
cards.notes:
BOTH commands MUST exist in plugin.yml or getCommand() returns null (NPE on setExecutor):
commands:
  spawn:
    description: Teleport to spawn
  setspawn:
    description: Set spawn
Also set api-version: "1.21" at top level. Location implements ConfigurationSerializable, so getConfig().set("spawn", location) + getConfig().getLocation("spawn") round-trips it (including world name, yaw, pitch) — do NOT hand-serialize x/y/z unless you want human-editable config. getLocation() returns null if the key is missing AND its getWorld() is null if that world isn't loaded — check both. Prefer Paper's teleportAsync() over teleport(): it loads the destination chunk off the main thread first (no lag spike, works across worlds); call it FROM the main thread, the future completes on the main thread. Classic mistakes: forgetting saveConfig() (change lost on restart), and legacy ChatColor strings instead of Adventure Components.

cards.title: Teleport a player to another world (nether/end) by world name
cards.notes: Bukkit.getWorld(name) returns null when the name is wrong or the world isn't loaded — ALWAYS null-check before building a Location, or you get 'World cannot be null'. Default world folder names are "world", "world_nether", "world_the_end" (they change if level-name in server.properties changes — enumerate with Bukkit.getWorlds() when unsure). Use teleportAsync (Paper) so the destination chunk is loaded off-thread; plain teleport() sync-loads the chunk and can lag the server. teleportAsync returns CompletableFuture<Boolean> — false means the teleport was cancelled (e.g. by a plugin event). Never call teleport/teleportAsync from an async task; schedule back to the main thread first.

cards.title: Apply, stack and remove potion effects on a player (timed and infinite)
cards.notes: Duration is in TICKS (20 = 1 second), a classic bug is passing seconds. Amplifier is 0-based: 0 = level I, 1 = level II. Use PotionEffect.INFINITE_DURATION (-1) for permanent effects — do NOT use Integer.MAX_VALUE (shows an ugly timer). 1.20.5+ renamed many constants to vanilla names: SLOW→SLOWNESS, JUMP→JUMP_BOOST, INCREASE_DAMAGE→STRENGTH, DAMAGE_RESISTANCE→RESISTANCE, FAST_DIGGING→HASTE, CONFUSION→NAUSEA — old names DO NOT compile on 1.21. Re-adding an effect of the same type replaces it if the new one is stronger/longer. The 6-arg constructor is (type, duration, amplifier, ambient, particles, icon) — particles=false hides swirls. addPotionEffect must run on the main thread.

cards.title: Per-player sidebar scoreboard that updates every second
cards.notes: Use getScoreboardManager().getNewScoreboard() per player — writing lines to getMainScoreboard() shows the SAME board to everyone and persists into world data. The only non-deprecated register overload on 1.21 is registerNewObjective(String, Criteria, Component) — the (String, String) and String-displayName ones are deprecated. registerNewObjective throws IllegalArgumentException if the name is already registered on that Scoreboard, hence the cache + computeIfAbsent. Lines are plain-String entries; each entry must be UNIQUE on the board (two lines with identical text collapse into one — pad with invisible chars or make text differ). Score value only controls ordering (higher = nearer the top). resetScores() before rewriting avoids stale lines. Paper 1.20.4+: obj.numberFormat(io.papermc.paper.scoreboard.numbers.NumberFormat.blank()) hides the red numbers on the right. Scoreboard API is main-thread only — never update from an async task.

cards.title: Adventure BossBar countdown shown to a player, updating name and progress
cards.notes: On Paper use net.kyori.adventure.bossbar.BossBar with player.showBossBar/hideBossBar — NOT the legacy org.bukkit.boss.BossBar / Bukkit.createBossBar (String-based, deprecated path). progress() MUST be within 0.0–1.0 or Adventure throws IllegalArgumentException — clamp computed values. Mutating the bar (name/progress/color) updates it live for every viewer; one bar instance can be shown to many players (great for global events). Always hideBossBar on PlayerQuitEvent and in onDisable, otherwise the bar sticks around after /reload. BukkitRunnable.cancel() inside run() stops the timer; runTaskTimer(plugin, delay, period) is in ticks.

cards.title: Spawn a custom mob with modified attributes, name and equipment (boss zombie)
cards.notes: Use the Consumer overload of spawn(): it configures the entity BEFORE it is added to the world (so spawn events and other plugins already see the final mob). Attribute constant names changed in 1.21.2+: it is Attribute.MAX_HEALTH / MOVEMENT_SPEED / ATTACK_DAMAGE — the old GENERIC_MAX_HEALTH etc. DO NOT compile on 1.21.4 (Attribute is now an interface with constants, not the old enum). Raising MAX_HEALTH does NOT heal the mob — call setHealth() afterwards or it spawns at 20 HP. getAttribute() returns null for attributes the mob type doesn't have. customName(Component) is the Paper/Adventure method (setCustomName(String) is deprecated). setPersistent(true) prevents natural despawning. Spawning must happen on the main thread — never from an async task.

cards.title: Play a sound and spawn particles (flame + colored dust) at a location
cards.notes: world.playSound broadcasts to everyone in hearing range; use player.playSound(...) with the same arguments to target one player only. Pitch is clamped to 0.5–2.0. Particle names were renamed in 1.20.5 to vanilla ids: REDSTONE→DUST, VILLAGER_HAPPY→HAPPY_VILLAGER, EXPLOSION_LARGE→EXPLOSION, SPELL_WITCH→WITCH — old names DO NOT compile on 1.21. Particle.DUST requires a Particle.DustOptions data object as the last argument (size 0.01–4.0), otherwise the server throws at runtime. In spawnParticle the 3 offsets are the random spread (a gaussian radius, NOT an exact offset) and 'extra' is usually particle speed. Sound and Particle became interfaces backed by registries in 1.21.3+ — you can't switch over them like enums anymore, but the constants work the same.

cards.title: Set world time (day/night) and weather (clear/rain/thunder) with durations
cards.notes: Time and weather are PER WORLD — setting them on "world" does not touch the nether/end or other loaded worlds. setTime uses ticks 0–24000: 0=sunrise, 1000=day, 6000=noon, 13000=night, 18000=midnight (it keeps the day counter; setFullTime overwrites the absolute tick count and can break daylight-sensitive logic). To force clear skies you must set BOTH setStorm(false) and setThundering(false); then setClearWeatherDuration(ticks) locks it so the natural weather cycle doesn't rain again immediately. Durations are in ticks (20/second). If gamerule doDaylightCycle is false the time freezes at whatever you set. All of these must run on the main thread.

cards.title: Simple economy: per-player balance stored in balances.yml + /pay command
cards.notes:
plugin.yml MUST declare the command or getCommand("pay") returns null:
commands:
  pay:
    description: Send money to a player
    usage: /pay <player> <amount>
Key balances by UUID, NEVER by player name (names change; name keys silently duplicate accounts). YamlConfiguration.loadConfiguration never returns null — a missing file just yields an empty config, so getDouble's default doubles as the starting balance. getConfig() is only for config.yml; a separate data file needs its own File + save(file), and mkdirs() on the data folder first (it doesn't exist on first run). Validate amount > 0 or players /pay themselves negative amounts to steal. Bukkit.getPlayerExact avoids the prefix-matching surprises of getPlayer. Saving on every transaction is fine for small servers; for busy ones batch saves on a timer or async (file IO only — never touch Bukkit API async). Always save in onDisable.

cards.title: Identify a custom item reliably (PersistentDataContainer tag, not display name)
cards.notes: NEVER identify a custom item by comparing its display name — Components have no getString()/getText(); name comparisons break with italics/color and players can rename items at an anvil. The robust pattern: stamp a PersistentDataContainer tag when creating the item, then check the tag in listeners. NamespacedKey should be created once with the plugin instance. Adventure Components do NOT have .getString(); if you truly need plain text use PlainTextComponentSerializer (see events-component-plaintext).

cards.title: Convert an Adventure Component to plain text (PlainTextComponentSerializer)
cards.notes: Adventure Components have NO getString()/getText() method — inventing one is a classic compile error. Use PlainTextComponentSerializer.plainText().serialize(component). It ships with Paper (no extra dependency). For chat input you usually want this to compare what a player typed. Prefer PDC tags over name comparison for identifying custom items (see items-inv-custom-item-pdc).
